events.what: Lazar claims the Littlewood conjecture for a restricted class of badly-approximable pairs; v2 (19 April 2025) is described as 'minor changes, improved main result'
Algorithm refining numerical upper-bound estimates in the Littlewood conjecture (Experimental Mathematics; received 8 April 2024)
Disproof of the uniform Littlewood conjecture, a distinct stronger variant
Higher-dimensional logarithmic obstruction for multiplicatively badly approximable vectors; substantive v3 on 17 January 2024

judgement.doubts: Lazar's first written argument is February 2022; the only evidence of new content in v2 is the arXiv comment 'minor changes, improved main result', which does not show new mathematics. Even if v2 were counted, it settles a restricted class of pairs (a case), so it would give partial, never claimed. The Matala-Aho–Törmä–Vapa paper was read only through snippets; it looks like numerical estimates for specific pairs (instances), and its 2024 year-only date cannot be placed relative to the snapshot.

corrections.why: F7/F1: Lazar's preprint dates to 3 Feb 2022; the record says the 2025 v2 is 'minor changes' with no diff showing new mathematics. Even if dated 2025, a restricted class of pairs is a case (partial), not claimed. The other events are variants (uniform Littlewood, higher dimensions) or numerical instances. A pre-snapshot partial result is not open_stale, so the status is open.
